answer: Each agent may claim rewards only after locking a stake that is slashed if independent audits show it copied another identity’s work or failed a randomly assigned task. The protocol caps rewards per stake-weighted identity and delays withdrawals through a challenge window, so splitting one operator across a nebula of accounts does not multiply payouts: each account needs separate capital at risk. A terrace of audit records gives challengers evidence, while a beacon signals which claims are under review. The attacker pays in locked funds and time, and risks losing both.
